name: Research Design Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday research design work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical research design tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday research design work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical research design tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about research design explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen research design approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. Keep research design changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Before starting research design work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. When research design decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Check that research design terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. Measure before optimizing any research design bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting research design assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated research design concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of research design correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these research design guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
